2027-01-17.title: Second Sunday after Denho
readings: Jesus returns to Galilee in the power of the Spirit
I am the Lord who sanctifies you
Wisdom at the beginning of creation
He shall feed his flock in the strength of the Lord
Look to the rock from which you were hewn
Be holy, for I am holy
2027-01-17.alt: Season of Denho. Mar Antonios of Egypt; name day of Thomas Mar Antonios. The Nineveh fast (three days) is from Monday 18 to Wednesday 20 January 2027, concluding on Thursday 21.
2027-01-17.verse: Very truly, I tell you, you will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.
theo: Philip finds Nathanael and tells him: “We have found him about whom Moses in the law and also the prophets wrote, Jesus son of Joseph from Nazareth.” Nathanael is sceptical: “Can anything good come out of Nazareth?” Philip does not argue. He says: “Come and see.” That is still the best way to bring someone to Christ: not debate, but an invitation to meet him.

Jesus knows Nathanael before they meet: “I saw you under the fig tree.” Nathanael's doubt turns into faith: “Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!” And Jesus promises more: “You will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.” Jacob dreamed of a ladder between heaven and earth (Genesis 28:12); Jesus says he himself is that ladder, the meeting place of God and humanity.

Proverbs presents Wisdom, present with God “at the beginning of his work”, delighting in creation; “whoever finds me finds life”. The Fathers saw here the eternal Son, the Wisdom of God. Micah promises the ruler from Bethlehem who “shall feed his flock in the strength of the LORD”. Peter draws the consequence: “as he who called you is holy, be holy yourselves in all your conduct.”

Tomorrow the Nineveh fast begins. Jonah preached in Nineveh and the whole city repented in sackcloth and ashes. The three days of fasting prepare us for the Great Fast. Like Nathanael, we are invited to come and see; like the Ninevites, to turn back to God with our whole heart.
conn: John 1:51 recalls Genesis 28:12: Christ is the true Bethel, the house of God and gate of heaven.
Proverbs 8:22–31 speaks of Wisdom present at creation; John 1:1–3 and Colossians 1:15–17 see in Christ the Word through whom all things were made.
“Look to the rock from which you were hewn” (Isaiah 51:1): our faith has roots in Abraham and Sarah, and in the apostles.
Leviticus 22:32 (“I am the LORD; I sanctify you”) is the root of 1 Peter 1:16: “You shall be holy, for I am holy.”
altar: “You will see heaven opened.” At every Holy Qurbono heaven opens over the altar: the angels join our worship and the Son of Man comes down to us in his Body and Blood.
outline: Ask: who first invited you to know Jesus?
The way of evangelisation: invitation and encounter, not argument.
“I saw you under the fig tree.” God knows us before we know him.
Christ is Jacob's ladder; the Qurbono is heaven on earth.
Three days of fasting, prayer and repentance, as preparation for the Great Fast.
live: Invite one friend, colleague or relative to Qurbono, a retreat or a prayer meeting.
Monday to Wednesday: fasting, the special prayers, and confession of sins.
Be holy in one thing (1 Peter 1:15)
Choose one area of conduct (speech, honesty, purity) to make holy this week.
fathers: Nathanael under the fig tree: Christ saw him before Philip called him, as he sees each of us under the shade of sin before grace calls us (Tractates on John 7).
Proverbs 8 speaks of the Son, the Wisdom of the Father, through whom all things were made, and who became man for our sake (Against the Arians II).
magis: Evangelisation person to person: a friendly conversation that invites the other to encounter Christ.
Seasons of penance in the liturgical year are intense moments of the Church's penitential practice.
All the faithful are called to the fullness of Christian life and to holiness.
saints: 17 Jan: St Antony of Egypt. 18–20 Jan: the Nineveh fast. 18–25 Jan: the Week of Prayer for Christian Unity. 20 Jan: St Sebastian. 21 Jan: St Agnes.
2027-01-17.prayer: Lord Jesus, you saw Nathanael under the fig tree and opened heaven before him. Help us to say “Come and see” to those who do not know you, and in these days of the Nineveh fast turn our hearts back to you, that we may be holy as you are holy. Amen.

quick: “Come and see”: the best way to bring someone to Christ.
Christ is the ladder between heaven and earth.
The Nineveh fast begins tomorrow: return to God.
2027-01-17.action: Invite one person to “come and see” this week.
2027-01-17.question: Whom can I invite to come and see Jesus?
2027-01-17.special: Second Sunday after Denho. Remind the faithful: the Nineveh fast (three days) is from Monday 18 to Wednesday 20 January, with the special prayers and abstinence.
illus: A young engineer in the Gulf stopped going to church for years. A colleague never argued with him, but every Friday said, “Come with me to Qurbono, just once.” One day he came, and he still goes. “Come and see” is still how faith spreads.

family.explain: Philip told Nathanael about Jesus. Nathanael was not sure, so Philip said: “Come and see!” When Nathanael met Jesus, he believed.
family.intention: We pray for friends and relatives who have drifted away from the Church.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we keep the Nineveh fast together as a family?”

catechism: Many forms of penance; the Nineveh fast.
kidsaint: A young man who heard the Gospel “sell what you own and give to the poor” and did it. He went to pray in the desert, and many came to learn from him. Lesson: when you hear God's Word, do it.
term: Three days of fasting before the Great Fast, recalling the repentance of Nineveh at Jonah's preaching (Jonah 3). The Malankara lectionary asks for special prayers, prostrations and abstinence in these days.
termMore: Jesus himself said “Come and see” to his first disciples (John 1:39); Philip repeats it to Nathanael. Faith passes from friend to friend.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you saw Nathanael under the fig tree before he came to you. You know us too. Open heaven to us as we gather. Amen.
share: Can anything good come out of Nazareth? (John 1:46). Whom do I write off too quickly?
I saw you under the fig tree (John 1:48). Do I believe Jesus knows me personally?
Be holy, for I am holy (1 Peter 1:16). What step toward holiness can I take this week?
interc: For the Church, that she may be holy in all her members.
For those who doubt, that they may come and see.
For our preparation for the Nineveh fast, which begins tomorrow.
For Christian unity, as the Unity Octave begins.
For our group, that we may bring others to Jesus as Philip brought Nathanael.
pm.close: Father, your Son reveals heaven opened to those who believe. Make us holy and send us to bring others to him. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today's Gospel tells how one friend brought another to Jesus. Philip found Nathanael and said: “We have found the one Moses and the prophets wrote about: Jesus of Nazareth.” Nathanael laughed: “Can anything good come out of Nazareth?”

Philip did not argue. He simply said: “Come and see.” That is still the best way to bring people to Christ. Not long debates, not pressure, but an invitation: come and see. Come to Qurbono with me. Come to the prayer meeting. Meet him yourself.

When Nathanael came, Jesus said: “I saw you under the fig tree.” Jesus knew him already. Nathanael's doubt melted: “Rabbi, you are the Son of God!” And Jesus promised: “You will see heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.” He is Jacob's ladder; in him heaven and earth meet. At this altar, today, heaven opens.

Tomorrow the Nineveh fast begins. When Jonah preached, the whole city turned back to God. Let us keep these three days well: fasting, the special prayers, a good Confession. And this week, let each of us say to one person: “Come and see.” Amen.
kids: Children, Philip met Jesus and was so happy! He ran to his friend Nathanael and said: “Come and see Jesus!”
Nathanael came, and Jesus said: “I saw you under the fig tree.” Jesus knew him already! Nathanael believed.
Jesus knows you too, and loves you. Who can you invite to come and meet Jesus? Let's say: “Come and see!”

intro: Philip finds Nathanael and tells him about Jesus. Nathanael doubts: “Can anything good come out of Nazareth?” Philip does not argue; he invites: “Come and see.” Faith grows through encounter.

sub: Nathanael's question is honest; God is not afraid of our questions.
Wisdom promises that those who seek diligently will find.
The best answer to doubt is an invitation to meet Christ in Scripture, in the Qurbono and in a living community.
q: I love those who love me, and those who seek me diligently find me.
Nathanael said to him, “Can anything good come out of Nazareth?” Philip said to him, “Come and see.”
points.apply: Invite one person who has drifted away to come with you to Sunday Qurbono.

sub: Jesus praises Nathanael: “an Israelite in whom there is no deceit.”
God says: “I am the LORD; I sanctify you”: holiness begins with an honest heart.
Jesus already knew Nathanael under the fig tree; nothing is hidden from him.
q: You shall not profane my holy name, that I may be sanctified among the people of Israel: I am the LORD; I sanctify you.
When Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him, he said of him, “Here is truly an Israelite in whom there is no deceit!”
points.apply: Remove one falsehood from your life this week: a lie, a pretence, a double life.

points.h: Heaven opened: Christ is the ladder
sub: Jacob dreamed of a ladder with angels ascending and descending.
Jesus says: you will see heaven opened and angels on the Son of Man: he is the meeting place of heaven and earth.
In the Holy Qurbono heaven opens; we join the angels in praise.
q: And he dreamed that there was a ladder set up on the earth, the top of it reaching to heaven; and the angels of God were ascending and descending on it.
Very truly, I tell you, you will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.
points.apply: At the Sanctus, remember that you are singing with the angels.

concl: Nathanael moved from doubt to confession: “Rabbi, you are the Son of God!”
Let us come and see, let our hearts be without deceit, and find in Christ the open heaven.
2027-01-17.resolve: Read John 1:35–51 slowly once this week and ask: where is Jesus inviting me to “come and see”?
